items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: I noticed on 1945 when the war ended I was playing with Charlie Barnet’s band.

ctx.x: Well when did the business start to go downhill or to change for you guys?

Well to tell you the truth, in my youth I wasn’t very intelligent. All I had in my mind was playing the piano. I didn’t think politically, I didn’t think musically — well musically actually just for the band that I was playing with. And I didn’t know what was going on in the world actually. I wasn’t aware of all of those things. All I knew is I had to support a wife and a kid, and this is what basically took up time in my head. But funny you should say — the end of the war, I just looked at my book the other…
so young and stupid. Because if we had any brains we’d have said are you crazy? I’m going to carry my daughter on the bus on one-nighters?
